subject: BUG: burn-down's snapshot freshness guard measures the WRONG CLOCK — it checks when the snapshot was WRITTEN (always ~1s, the status line rewrites it every render) not how old the DATA is. Live proof 2026-08-15: ts=now but r7=2026-08-11T07:00Z and r5=2026-08-07, i.e. reset fields 4-8 days stale, usage 7d=38%/5d=30% while the owner's UI showed ~18%. Only the incidental 'left<=0 → window already rolled' check caught it; had r7 been slightly in the FUTURE with stale usage, burn-down would have forecast from garbage and could BURN wrongly. Fix candidates: treat a resets_at in the past as UNUSABLE data (not just 'rolled'), and/or refuse to forecast when the reset fields have not moved across N distinct writes.
done_when: burn-down holds with an explicit 'stale data' reason whenever the snapshot's window fields are inconsistent with its write time; a frozen payload can never produce a BURN; test covers reset-in-past AND reset-in-future-with-frozen-usage
seen: reproduced the live failure as a fixture (fresh ts + 8-day-old 5h reset + plausible 7d reset) and confirmed burn-down now HOLDs naming STALE instead of burning on it; also verified against the REAL snapshot after it refreshed — 7d 19%, 2.54d left, which matches the owner's UI and passes the new guard cleanly.
